reasons: The rule applies: Section 3.4(b) makes Customer pay 'early termination charges' on termination for convenience, which is exactly the Customer-payable termination/minimum-fee exposure the rule targets (no Vendor-payable service credit is at issue).

Deviation classification is correct: the charge is defined only by reference to Attachment A and Service Option Attachments with no cap anywhere in the Agreement, so it meets neither the preferred position (no Customer-payable LD) nor the fallback (capped at 3 months' fees as the sole liquidated amount).

The redline implements the fallback precisely and actionably — a 3-months'-charges aggregate cap with a stated calculation method, expressed as the sole amount payable and IBM's sole remedy — rather than over-reaching for outright deletion of an embedded priced term.
The high changed-character ratio is justified: capping an uncapped cross-referenced charge requires appending a proviso, and the original obligation language is left intact.
The comment is accurate and on-tone: it states the playbook position, offers the fallback, and correctly notes the Section 13.1 unilateral-change risk to Attachment A without lecturing.
